title: Power Management doesn't fall back to normal sleep if Sleep-then-hibernate set, and then hibernate is disabled
line: With sleep then hibernate or hybrid sleep chosen but no longer available, closing the lid or pressing the power or Sleep key now puts the computer to sleep instead of doing nothing.
explanation: The KCM hides sleep then hibernate and hybrid sleep once the system can't do them, but the old SleepMode stays in powerdevilrc. SuspendSession then asked for those modes anyway, and libkworkspace's SessionManagement silently ignores a request logind says it can't do, so the lid, power button, Sleep key and idle sleep did nothing. The change only uses those modes when the suspend controller reports them as possible and otherwise falls back to plain sleep.

commits.message:
suspendsession: Fall back to plain sleep if the sleep mode is unavailable

With "Standby, then hibernate" or "Hybrid sleep" set but no longer possible, for
example after hibernation was disabled, the lid, power button and Sleep key did
nothing. Use plain sleep in that case instead.

BUG: 500841
BUG: 498298

media.caption: Master, sleep then hibernate set with hibernation unavailable: Sleep key, power button and lid close make no suspend call at all
With the fix, the same three actions each suspend
Master, hybrid sleep set but unavailable: nothing happens either
With the fix, plain sleep each time

review.text: Minimal, well-placed fix in PowerDevil's SuspendSession::triggerImpl that checks canSuspendThenHibernate() and canHybridSuspend() before requesting those modes and falls back to plain suspend() when unavailable. Thoroughly verified against dbusmock logind and UPower for Sleep key, power button, and lid close across both available and unavailable configurations.

reviews.text: Minimal, well-placed fix in PowerDevil's SuspendSession::triggerImpl that checks canSuspendThenHibernate() and canHybridSuspend() before requesting those modes and falls back to plain suspend() when unavailable. Thoroughly verified against dbusmock logind and UPower for Sleep key, power button, and lid close across both available and unavailable configurations.

Minimal, correct fix at the right place: SuspendSession::triggerImpl now only asks for sleep-then-hibernate or hybrid sleep when the suspend controller (logind via SessionManagement) reports them possible, and otherwise does plain sleep, which is exactly the fallback the retitled bug asks for and the same cause as 498298's main report. The dbusmock logind timelines prove no call before and Suspend after for Sleep key, power button and lid with both stale modes, plus the regression check that available modes are still honoured. The only behaviour change, an explicit suspendHybrid D-Bus request sleeping instead of silently doing nothing when hybrid sleep is unavailable, is documented and preferable to a no-op.
